EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  APRIL 23, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 26, 2018
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER KEMP

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE FEBRUARY 26, 2018 ADJOURNED
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
A letter from Candace Ham, 26802 Rolling Hills Road, regarding her concerns about the
California Water Service Company water reliability project was reviewed.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE
WRITEN COMMUNICATION.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
MEMBER SHINN reported that there had been no project update meetings held by California
Water Service since the last Equestrian Committee meeting. MEMBER BRTIS indicated that
she had learned that the proposed installation of 20 pipe corrals on the PV Landfill adjacent to
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 23, 2018  1
 the rear of the Peter Weber Equestrian Center had been cancelled. The Community Services
Director responded that he disagreed, as having recently spoken with Mr. Houle about how he
was going to meet with nearby Roanwood Homeowners Association residents to assure them
that the temporary boarding would have little impact on their neighborhood.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

DRAFT TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET
The Community Services Director reviewed the draft Trail Safety Pamphlet and requested
comments and suggestions for its improvement. He noted that Sharon Yarber, PVP
Horsemens Association representative, Adrienne Mohan, PVP Land Conservancy
Conservation Director, and staff had collaborated to determine the content in this pamphlet. It
was suggested that all references to bicycles and bike logos should be removed.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CITY CELEBRATION VENUE UPDATE
The Community Services Director reported that Park and Activities Commission had voted
unanimously to make a recommendation to City Council to remain at Ernie Howlett Park for
the 2018 City Celebration event in collaboration with the Remember the Music Festival. He
noted to the Committee that following the 2016 City Celebration event at Howlett Park, during
the November 8, 2016 Joint City Council – Park and Activities Commission City Celebration
Debriefing Meeting, it had been determined that a substantially shorter event would be
planned for 2017 at Howlett Park (such as 9:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.). Unexpectedly,
representatives from Betty’s Foundation, who had held six prior indoor Music Festival to raise
funds for Alzheimer’s research, contacted City staff in February 2017 to see if they could hold
an afternoon through early evening family music festival in September 2017 in Howlett Park.
Thus, this is how the collaboration with the Music Festival started last year.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL stated that it was her belief that these were two distinct events, with
the Music Festival having its own annual following. Further, she felt that The Empty Saddle
Club had historically been a better place for the event. In addition, she heard that those who
trailered horses to Howlett Park found it challenging to get in and out of the park. Several
Equestrian Committee Members and members of the audience agreed. MEMBER SHINN
stated that she, MEMBER SILVANO, and Pam Schachter had tried to make the Howlett Park
Equestrian Center work for the past two years with no success in drawing spectators to watch
the equestrian games, trail course, or demonstrations. MEMBER KEMP indicated that
unfortunately it’s the logistics of Howlett Park’s location being so far away from the majority of
equestrians living in the central and eastern side of the City, which is closer to The Empty
Saddle Club.

MEMBER SILVANO reminded the Committee that the California Water Service Company
Water Reliability Project is expected to close trails on the east side of the City around the date
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 23, 2018  2
 of the 2018 City Celebration making it even more challenging for equestrians to ride to the
Howlett Park. MEMBER SHINN encouraged Committee Members to attend the April 24,
2018 City Council Meeting where the Park and Activities Commission’s recommendation
would be considered.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

CHANDLER PARK TEMPORARY VIDEO CAMERA UPDATE
As directed, the Community Services Director reported that several video surveillance
systems were investigated. He noted that this was being done due to the Equestrian
Committee’s mixed information regarding how busy Chandler Park arena was and the agenda
item regarding the potential construction of a second arena in Chandler Park.

Staff was able to find a reasonably priced, mobile video camera system which are normally
used temporarily on construction sites to monitor tools, equipment and project materials. In
response to his inquiry as to what 30-day period that it should monitor this arena, MEMBER
HARIK recommended May 15 to June 15, 2018 and several Members agreed.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE PROMOTIONS UPDATE
The Community Services Director distributed a lengthy list of methods being used to promote
the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride event. He thanked the PVP Horsemens Association members in
attendance for their assistance in contacting their membership multiple times. Audience
member Sean Martin stated that he was organizing a raffle on behalf of the PVPHA where all
riders would receive a raffle ticket for $50 gift card drawings after the breakfast event when
the equestrian games started in the Howlett Park arenas. Several MEMBERS reported
hearing from local equestrian groups and trainers that they were planning to participate this
year.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE MEETING UPDATE
Subcommittee Member SHINN reported how successful this first meeting was in starting off
the development and promotion of equine emergency preparedness and response in our City.
She was pleased that Lisa Eldridge, LA County Animal Care & Control and John Douglass,
ERT Trainer attended the meeting. The Community Services Director announced that there
were internal staff responsibility changes currently taking place in regards to the coordination
of the City’s emergency planning and overseeing all animal issues (coyotes, peafowl, equine,
dogs, etc.). The new staff person would soon be coordinating future Subcommittee meetings.
DRAFT EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 23, 2018  3
 MEMBER SHINN indicated that she would be working with Ms. Eldridge to contact those who
had attended the recent Equine Emergency Preparedness Workshop at Howlett Park that
indicated interest in taking the Equine Response Team Level 1 course. The Community
Services Director stated that the City could host the 4-hour class on a Saturday in the Council
Chambers whenever the training date was finalized.

MEMBER SHINN then highlighted the initial steps discussed at the Subcommittee Meeting
that will be pursued, including: 1) a trailer loading clinic lead by Sean Martin; 2) identifying and
contacting residents with horse trailers to see if they would be willing to participate during an
equine emergency evacuation; 3) offering a microchip clinic utilizing available funding from LA
County Animal Care & Control; and 4) for the Subcommittee to meet soon with the newly
assigned City staff member responsible for emergency planning and preparedness to discuss
educational methods for the equestrian community. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL thanked the
Subcommittee for coordinating these efforts.

MEMBER KEMP reported that he was unable to submit an Emergency Information Form to
our City’s Emergency Coordinator on the City’s website. The Community Services Director
indicated that he would notify the City staff members responsible for the collection of this
information about this issue.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THIS
AGENDA ITEM.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER KEMP reported that a PV Drive North Trail sign pole was down across from
  City Hall. MEMBER BRTIS stated that the new lighted equestrian/pedestrian crossing
  on Rolling Hills Road was not stopping drivers from driving through the crosswalk while
  riders or pedestrians were within it. MEMBER SHINN reported the same issue with the
  Palos Verdes Drive North lighted crosswalk near City Hall. At the request of
  Committee Members, the Community Services Director will notify the Assistant City
  Manager to have this issue addressed by the City’s Traffic and Safety Committee.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  EQUINE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE – Monthly

C.  TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET – May 29, 2018
DRAFT EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
APRIL 23, 2018  4
 D.  CITY CELEBRATION VENUE UPDATE – May 29, 2018

E.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE UPDATE – May 29, 2018

F.  CHANDLER PARK VIDEO SURVEILLANCE UPDATE – May 29, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:22 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
